dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24; dhāraṇā 82 = verses 105–106 and dhāraṇā 89 = verses 113–114, otherwise one verse each; dhāraṇā 112 = verse 137)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: nijadehe sarvadikkaṃ yugapad bhāvayed viyat | nirvikalpamanās tasya viyat sarvam pravartate ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, compared with Wallis's concordance, Pradīpaka and the Singh scan
dharana.rendering: Let one contemplate space (viyat) in every direction at once within one's own body. For one whose mind is free of thought-constructs, everything becomes space.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer (as printed in Wallis's concordance); not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh stresses two conditions: the contemplation must be simultaneous (yugapat), not direction by direction, and the mind must be still (nirvikalpamanāḥ); then one reaches the plane in which differences fall away. Wallis: 'everything becomes spacious'. Note: a previous House 1 draft of Door 014 carried this verse under hatha.es numbering; under Singh it belongs here.
dharana.technique_name: Space in Every Direction at Once, Within the Body
dharana.instruction: Feel space opening in every direction within the body at the same time.

verification.notes: Door index = Singh dhāraṇā number, read directly in Singh's own headings and cross-checked against The Mystery Within's Singh-numbered list and Wallis's concordance. Caveat: Singh was read from an OCR scan, not a print copy in hand.

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 43 does not specify a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

points: space opening in all directions at once
geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is a sphere: the body at its centre and space opening in every direction at the same moment, not one direction after another.
geometry.svg_hint: a seated outline drawn very faintly at the centre of a soft sphere with rays in all directions
geometry.honesty: Geometry records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Open in all directions
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: attention stops travelling from place to place and opens everywhere at once. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: wherever the breath naturally ends; this door places nothing on the breath
breath.cue: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps you settle, then let the count go. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Open in every direction at once, without picking a direction
orientation.gravity: Let the floor or chair carry the body completely; there is no posture to hold
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: Space in all directions within the body, felt simultaneously
attention.secondary: Thoughts left alone, so the openness can stay simple

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: Let one contemplate space (viyat) in every direction at once within one's own body. For one whose mind is free of thought-constructs, everything becomes space.
adiyogi.method_summary: Feel the body's inner space opening in every direction at once: front, back, sides, up and down together, not one after another. Let thoughts pass without following them, and rest in the openness.

honesty.disclosure: Door 020 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 20 (verse 43) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type is school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 020 is dharana 20, verse 43. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).
The seat, breath counts, reaction metaphor, attention-map drawing and beat scripts are school devices, not part of the verse.
The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.
No medical claims. Reaction names are metaphors, not biochemistry.
New door researched on 2026-10-06 on branch research/vbt-houses-2-7; awaiting guardian review.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. If the sense of openness feels unsettling, open the eyes and feel the contact of the body with the floor. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.

beats.title: Name the door
beats.script: This is Door 020: space in every direction at once, within the body. Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 20, verse 43.

beats.title: Geometry
beats.script: No shape to make. Sit or lie down. The map is a sphere, with you at the centre and space opening every way at once.

beats.title: Orientation
beats.script: Let the floor or the chair carry you. Eyes closed or soft.

beats.title: Breath
beats.script: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps. No forced hold.

beats.title: Attention
beats.script: Feel space inside the body opening in every direction together. Not one direction, then the next. All at once.

beats.title: Reaction cue
beats.script: School image: a narrow focus opening into a sphere. A metaphor, not medicine.

beats.title: Adiyogi thread
beats.script: Verse 43: contemplate space in all directions at once within your own body; with a thought-free mind, everything becomes space.

beats.title: Exit / integrate
beats.script: Let the practice go. Take one free breath. Open the eyes and look around the room.
